observation.description: The guide teaches authRequestCode/authExchange with 'the code is read from the server's admin-gated mailbox' but never shows how to read it: the mailbox route appears only as a bare row in the capability index, its required x-snapback-impersonation-capability header (the dev.ready.json.impersonation sidecar) is named nowhere, SNAPBACK_AUTH_IMPERSONATION_REQUIRED does not say how to supply the capability (unlike the exemplary auth-protocol diagnostic, which names its exact header), and the working multi-persona recipe — request-code, mailbox with admin token + impersonation capability, exchange, then an external-bearer SnapbackClient with the five protocol offers — had to be learned from the packaged comparator-profile.mjs bytes (recorded as an assistance event). Constructing a bare client with authClientProtocol: 1 also refuses ('requires browser, agent, or explicit external-bearer custody') without pointing at createExternalSessionClient. Once known, the recipe is excellent: three real bearer-backed principals in ~100ms each.

competitorOutcome.description: The frozen Convex arm's biggest ceremony was auth fixtures (custom JWT issuer, JWKS, key custody). Snapback's minted-session dev path is materially lighter — but only discoverable today by reading package internals, which forfeits the differentiator.

mustNotRegress: The three-authority gate on the mailbox and mint paths (admin token + process-bound impersonation capability + non-production), and the refusal to let a browser hold any of them.
smallestCoherentFix: A guide section (sessions-and-principals or testing/acceptance) with the complete dev/test persona recipe — mailbox route, exact header names, sidecar location, createExternalSessionClient — plus SNAPBACK_AUTH_IMPERSONATION_REQUIRED naming its expected carrier the way the auth-protocol diagnostic does.
acceptanceWitness: A cold external agent following only the guide mints two personas and passes a cross-principal acceptance check without reading any package or repository source; the diagnostic's message names the header.
